source.title: Parseval Regularization for Continual Reinforcement Learning
source.authors: Wesley Chung; Lynn Cherif; D. Meger; D. Precup

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; no apparent truncation or corruption relevant to the study.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests Parseval regularization in continual reinforcement learning and reports training and optimization outcomes. Its own experiments do not test whether large randomly initialized classifiers reach zero or near-zero training classification error, nor the conditions named in V1–V6. Mentions of initialization research and the 10,000-layer CNN are background citations.
record.gate_note: The paper reports performance profiles, learning curves, network-property measurements and initialization ablations, but none measures the training classification error or tests a version of the claim. Cited prior-work results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses orthogonal initialization and its proposed optimization benefits to motivate Parseval regularization, then evaluates continual RL performance and network diagnostics. It does not test V1–V6. Appendix A varies initialization scale and rank in shallow networks, but does not compare activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, or trainable depth.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that Parseval regularization improves continual RL performance while preserving favorable network properties. They also emphasize that its capacity constraint can be relaxed with diagonal layers or input scaling, and that initialization scale and rank have complex relationships with performance.
record.recipe_differences: The study's intervention is Parseval regularization in continual reinforcement learning. Its initialization and deep-network statements are cited background, not experiments testing the listed recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: Parseval regularization improves continual RL success rates and returns across Gridworld, CARL and MetaWorld benchmarks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Maintaining approximately orthogonal weights during training can improve adaptation across sequences of RL tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix A.1 reports little performance effect from increasing initialization scale up to 8, and a nonmonotonic relationship between initial rank and performance on single MetaWorld tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization scale and rank have setting-dependent effects on learning in shallow RL networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix A.2 reports similar performance with gains of 1 and square root of 2 under Parseval regularization in shallow networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These two initialization gains perform similarly in the tested shallow continual RL setting with Parseval regularization.

fits_no_version.finding: Parseval regularization maintains higher stable rank, lower neuron weight correlation and a tighter spread of squared input-output Jacobian entries.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Orthogonality regularization preserves these network diagnostics during continual RL training.

record.problems: The study's own results concern continual RL performance and network properties rather than classification training error. Statements about the listed initialization and deep-network methods are citations to prior work.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows: all reported experimental outcomes concern continual RL benchmarks or network diagnostics outside the claim versions; cited prior-study findings are excluded.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels.
Spurious local minima and extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-related training degradation, identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization alternatives.
Activation-matched initialization improving learning speed or trainable depth; orthogonal versus equal-variance Gaussian initialization; very deep convolutional training.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, catapult dynamics, sharpness evolution and divergence.
Batch normalization improving training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and normalization-free Fixup residual training.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation should change from tests to uses_without_test and its tranche from T6 to T4. Layer normalization comparisons do not test batch normalization. Width comparisons do not measure teacher-student local minima. The omitted experiments are already declared in rows_left_out, so they require no missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels; effects of model size, training duration, early stopping and regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiments, spurious local minima, and effects of student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual networks, depth-related training error, batch normalization, and the cited special initialization and normalization-free residual recipes.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, depth, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and 10,000-layer convolutional classification training.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss and curvature dynamics, sharpness, and divergence in the specified squared-loss or full-batch settings.
Batch normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance for the specified MNIST, CIFAR-10 and ImageNet systems; Fixup residual training.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
